item.title: ssl-proxy: drop
item.description:
Nixpkgs version was unmaintained since February 2024. Upstream is unmaintained since March 2025.

In nixpkgs we pin a commit with a go lock pulling go crypto from 2022 [1]. Current upstream master branch is only slightly less horrible, pinning 0.36.0 [2] from 2025-03-05 [3].

Noone should be running questionably outdated reverse proxy software. Considering upstream is dead [4],[5], removal from nixpkgs is sensible.

[1] https://github.com/suyashkumar/ssl-proxy/blob/6b0f364be9bbf0de46520a6b85d30792fcc3cb80/go.mod#L7 [2] https://github.com/suyashkumar/ssl-proxy/blob/7cf7ab6b7bb433c013e0eefc00e95536a9248047/go.mod#L7 [3] https://go.googlesource.com/crypto/+/refs/tags/v0.36.0 [4] https://github.com/suyashkumar/ssl-proxy/pulls [5] https://github.com/suyashkumar/ssl-proxy/commits/master/

item.title: angie: 1.12.3 -> 1.12.4
item.description:
Description of changes

Bump angie from 1.12.3 to 1.12.4. Two lines change in pkgs/servers/http/angie/default.nix, the version and the source hash. Nothing else moves, and both local patches still apply to the new tree, nix-etag-1.15.4.patch at the same offsets as on 1.12.3 and nix-skip-check-logs-path.patch unchanged.

This is a security-only release. Angie 1.12.4 ports five fixes from nginx 1.31.7 (release notes, tag):

  • CVE-2026-93479, variables in the root or log_format directives could cause worker process memory corruption or a worker process crash.
  • CVE-2026-97629, ssl_session_cache with the shared parameter and no ssl_session_ticket_key directive let an attacker forge a TLS session and bypass client certificate verification.
  • CVE-2026-95101, proxying over HTTP/3 could treat part of an unknown frame as the request body, bypassing client_max_body_size or injecting data into the proxied request.
  • CVE-2026-15176, the alias directive combined with a URI-changing rewrite and a later evaluation of $request_filename could cause memory corruption or a worker process crash.
  • CVE-2026-97205, SSI with include virtual commands under asynchronous file I/O could cause memory corruption or a worker process crash.

Impact for Nixpkgs. Unlike the 1.12.2 bump, these are not gated behind one OpenSSL build. The default angie build compiles --with-http_ssl_module, --with-http_v3_module, --with-file-aio and --with-threads, so four of the five are reachable in a default build whenever the triggering configuration is used. The exception is CVE-2026-97205, which needs the SSI module, and nixpkgs does not compile --with-http_ssi_module into the default angie build.

This is a security release, so a backport to release-26.05 is warranted.

Test results

Built and tested from this branch on x86_64-linux:

  • nix build .#angie builds 1.12.4 with both local patches applied.
  • nix-build -A angie.passthru.tests builds all three tests, 64 must succeed steps across them and 0 failures, with the three VM runs finishing in 7.39 s, 9.87 s and 10.31 s. The angie-api test includes the assertion that .angie.version reports 1.12.4, and angie-http3 covers HTTP/3 200 and 404.
  • No Test failed, no FAIL and no Traceback in the transcript.

AI assistance. The change and the build and test runs are the submitter's. This text was drafted with Hermes Agent (deepseek-v4.1-flash) from those verified results and reviewed by the submitter before posting.
